pure-announcement.rationale: It is hung on the KubeCon beta launch but goes far past it — architecture, CNI-collision caveats, header-enrichment policy design, and the OBI/Hubble/Tetragon role-split are transferable coverage of the zero-code eBPF technique.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts are MCP-governance and vulnerability-format notes; nothing in the supplied set covers eBPF-based zero-code observability.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims are sourced to the OpenTelemetry docs, the OBI GitHub repo, and the Splunk KubeCon announcement, and the deployment behaviour is reproducible on any cluster.

durability.rationale: The spine of the note is the pre-1.0 moment — v0.8.0, beta status, a late-2026 GA roadmap at '60% of the checklist', and config keys the author warns v0 minors may break — so much of it goes stale within twelve months even though the kernel-capture/user-space-parse mechanism endures.

actionability.rationale: The adoption checklist, the run-OBI-alongside-Hubble/Tetragon role split, tail-sampling and default-redaction recommendations, and the OBI-vs-Pixie/Beyla decision table directly change how a team would build its observability stack.

atomicity.rationale: Despite its length it argues one idea — vendor-neutral zero-code L7 instrumentation from the kernel via OTLP, run alongside SDKs and network/security eBPF tools — and everything else is supporting detail for that adoption decision.
